data.cultural_impact: The name Ram has a rich cultural history in Hinduism, being the name of one of the most revered deities in the Hindu pantheon. The epic Ramayana, one of the two major Sanskrit epics of ancient India, revolves around Lord Rama. The character Rama is often depicted as the ideal man, embodying qualities such as truthfulness, obedience to elders, righteousness, and courage. The name Ram is used in daily life among Hindu communities, and often given as a name to newborn babies.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hindu spirituality, Lord Rama is considered to be an incarnation of the god Vishnu, who came to protect dharma (righteousness) and to provide salvation to his devotees. The name Ram is believed to bring not just material wealth and success, but also spiritual growth and enlightenment. The name Ram is considered a sacred invocation in Hindu spirituality, and is often used during meditation and worship. The mantra "So Hum Ram So Hum" is a popular chant used to connect with Lord Rama, and to inspire thoughts of divinity and self-realization.

historical_references.reference: Ramayana, an ancient Indian epic, mentions a king named Rama, who is considered an incarnation of the god Vishnu.
